findings.reason: The revised two-answer set is complete: NaN risk and an explicit row policy are valid, while finite-minimum and float32-only guarantees are false.
findings.evidence: For an all--infinity row, naive max subtraction computes -infinity - -infinity. A finite equal sentinel can normalize to a semantically invalid nonzero distribution, and float32 testing does not establish behavior for half/bfloat16 or fused kernels.
findings.sourceLocator: Reference implementation uses -infinity mask bias followed by softmax; notes on backend and precision differences
